workup.reason_code_summary: The issuer alleges the cardholder cancelled their FluxFit subscription on 18 March 2025 and was still billed GBP 29.99 on 20 April 2025. To defend under Visa 13.2 the merchant must prove all four of the following: terms disclosing recurring billing and how to cancel, advance notice of the upcoming charge, no cancellation request before the billing date, and the cardholder's original opt-in to recurring billing.

pointers.quote: Subscriptions auto-renew monthly at the rate disclosed at signup until cancelled. Members may cancel at any time via their account dashboard or by emailing support@fluxfit.example.

requirements.reasoning: The terms disclose monthly auto-renewal and two cancellation methods. They are version terms_v3.2, published February 2025, and nothing shows this version was in force when the cardholder signed up.

pointers.quote: Members will be notified by email at least 5 days prior to each renewal.

requirements.reasoning: This is a policy statement only. There is no email, send log or delivery record showing a reminder was sent to this cardholder before the 20 April 2025 charge, and the stated 5-day window is shorter than the typical 7+ days. Whether GBP 29.99 is above the notification threshold is not established.

The merchant has supplied no account history, cancellation log or support-ticket search showing that no cancellation was received before 20 April 2025. The cardholder specifically claims to have cancelled on 18 March 2025.

There is no signup record, checkbox or consent log, or initial transaction evidence showing the cardholder opted in to recurring billing. The generic terms document does not prove this cardholder accepted it.

workup.action_justification: Only one of four required elements is satisfied, and the missing items (cancellation log, reminder email record, opt-in record) are system records the merchant should be able to supply.
evidence_to_request: Full account activity and cancellation log for the cardholder's account, covering signup to the present, showing no cancellation via the dashboard before 20 April 2025.
Search results from the support@fluxfit.example mailbox and ticketing system for any contact from the cardholder between 1 March and 20 April 2025, specifically around 18 March 2025.
The renewal reminder email sent for the 20 April 2025 charge, with send timestamp, recipient address and delivery status from the email platform log.
The signup/opt-in record: signup date, IP and timestamp, the recurring-billing consent checkbox or acceptance record, and the terms version accepted at signup.
If signup predates February 2025, the terms version in force at signup showing the recurring billing and cancellation disclosures.
The cardholder's billing history (prior renewal dates and amounts), to establish the billing cycle.
workup.rationale: FluxFit Online's published terms (terms_v3.2) disclose monthly auto-renewal and cancellation via the account dashboard or email. The merchant has not provided evidence that a renewal notice was sent to this cardholder before the 20 April 2025 charge. It has not provided a record showing that no cancellation was received before that date. It has not provided the cardholder's original opt-in to recurring billing. The case does not meet the all-four requirement of Visa 13.2 and is pending the merchant's account, cancellation, notification and signup records.
caveats: The cardholder cites a specific cancellation date (18 March 2025). If the merchant's logs or support inbox show any contact on or around that date, the charge is indefensible and liability should be accepted.

The terms say cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing period. If billing runs on the 20th, a 18 March cancellation would end the subscription around 20 March, so the 20 April charge would still be after cancellation. This clause does not help the merchant here.
The terms promise only 5 days' notice, not the typical 7+ days. Confirm the applicable notification threshold for a GBP 29.99 UK transaction.
The terms document was published February 2025 and states it applies to all members. It is a policy document, not proof this cardholder saw or accepted it. Signup may predate this version.
AVS Y, CVV M and frictionless 3DS confirm card authentication but are not relevant to whether the subscription was cancelled.
The transaction timestamp of 2025-04-20T00:00:01Z indicates an automated renewal run, which is consistent with a recurring charge.

rule_text:
Visa 13.2 - Cancelled Recurring Transaction
Issuer claim: Cardholder cancelled a recurring subscription but was still charged.
Logic: ALL 4 requirements must be satisfied.
Compelling evidence requirements:
  1. Terms of service disclosing the recurring billing arrangement and the cancellation method
  2. Evidence the cardholder was notified of the upcoming charge (typically 7+ days in advance) for transactions over a defined threshold
  3. No record of the cardholder having submitted a cancellation request prior to the billing date
  4. Evidence of the cardholder's original opt-in to the recurring arrangement
prechecks: AVS: Y (full address match); CVV: M (match); 3DS: frictionless
Shipping vs billing postcode: no shipping postcode on file (digital goods or service)
Chargeback raised 15 days after the transaction
